metadata.purpose: Finite documentary mapping, not an acceptance verdict

rows.requirement: As a Host developer, I want MiniMax to have its own Provider identity, so that routing identifies the actual service operator.
As a Host developer, I want Responses through the existing Client, so that I can keep my Responses integration.
As a Host developer, I want Chat Completions through the existing Client, so that I can keep my Chat integration.
As a Host developer, I want Messages through the existing Client, so that I can keep my Messages integration.
As a Host developer, I want Stream and Complete on every route, so that delivery style does not change supported behavior.
As a Host developer, I want StreamSimple and CompleteSimple on every route, so that protocol-neutral callers can use MiniMax.
As a Host developer, I want existing protocol options and hooks retained, so that I do not need a parallel MiniMax request API.
As a Host developer, I want incorrect protocol options rejected, so that a Binding change cannot reinterpret my request.
As a tenant administrator, I want separate protocol Bindings, so that authorization is explicit for every route.
As a tenant administrator, I want denied models rejected before credential access, so that unauthorized requests cannot read secrets.
As a tenant administrator, I want immutable Binding and Credential Snapshots, so that retries cannot change account or purpose.
As a tenant administrator, I want shared Clients to isolate tenant accounts, so that concurrent requests cannot mix credentials.
As a Host operator, I want China and international identities distinguished, so that regional service assumptions are not mixed.
As a Host operator, I want standard and M Plan credentials configured explicitly, so that quota purpose is known before a call.
As a Host operator, I want missing model entitlement reported honestly, so that another model's success cannot certify availability.
As a Host developer, I want independent model entries per protocol, so that one protocol's defaults cannot alter another's behavior.
As a Host developer, I want M3 and M3.1 configured independently, so that their reasoning constraints remain accurate.
As a Host developer, I want the first release's text-only subset stated clearly, so that upstream vision support is not mistaken for implemented input support.
As a Host developer, I want omitted reasoning to keep each protocol's documented default, so that absence is not reinterpreted as disabled thinking.
As a Host developer, I want M3 Chat thinking enabled by default, so that I retain the endpoint's intended behavior.
As a Host developer, I want M3 Responses and Messages thinking disabled by default, so that enabling reasoning remains an explicit choice.
As a Host developer, I want M3.1's mandatory thinking enforced, so that no entry point silently sends an invalid off request.
As a Host developer, I want M3.1's five supported depths, so that I can select the intended reasoning effort.
As a Host developer, I want M3 exposed as a thinking switch rather than artificial depth levels, so that controls do what they claim.
As a Host developer, I want full unsupported levels rejected and simple levels resolved predictably, so that reasoning selection is understandable.
As a Host developer, I want canonical levels separate from wire fields, so that sampling selection does not masquerade as measured model intensity.
As a Host developer, I want reasoning separated from visible answers where supported, so that my UI can present both correctly.
As a Host developer, I want M3's actual reasoning format preserved, so that conflicting documentation cannot corrupt history.
As a Host developer, I want tools on all three protocols, so that the Host can continue its existing tool loop.
As a Host developer, I want fragmented tool arguments assembled once, so that progress is observable without executing incomplete input.
As a Host developer, I want multiple tool calls kept distinct, so that arguments and results cannot be paired with the wrong call.
As a Host developer, I want reasoning and tool calls replayed together, so that subsequent generations retain required context.
As a Host developer, I want unsupported forced tool selection rejected, so that requested constraints are not weakened to auto.
As a Host developer, I want ignored parallel controls rejected when I depend on them, so that successful calls cannot imply an unenforced guarantee.
As a Host developer, I want complete Responses history replay, so that I do not depend on provider-side saved state.
As a Host developer, I want Responses input and output reasoning shapes checked independently, so that SDK decoding does not imply valid replay.
As a Host developer, I want authoritative final output reconciled with deltas, so that text and reasoning are neither lost nor duplicated.
As a Host developer, I want Messages thinking signatures retained, so that native continuation follows the provider contract.
As a tenant administrator, I want persisted Native State trusted only by the Host, so that client-supplied signatures do not grant replay authority.
As a tenant administrator, I want cross-account and cross-protocol history downgraded safely, so that account-specific state cannot cross a boundary.
As a Host developer, I want tool identifiers treated as opaque values, so that punctuation and long IDs cannot break pairing.
As a Host developer, I want protocol-specific output budgets, so that invalid fields or hidden budget inflation cannot change my request.
As a Host developer, I want reasoning-only truncation reported as truncation, so that an empty answer is not fabricated into success.
As a Host developer, I want final usage read after content stops, so that late usage chunks are not discarded.
As a Host developer, I want missing usage distinguished from reported zero, so that unknown consumption is not shown as free.
As a Host developer, I want cache and reasoning tokens normalized by protocol, so that estimates do not double count them.
As a Host developer, I want automatic cache usage retained, so that available cache savings remain observable.
As a tenant administrator, I want cache routing keys scoped to tenant and account, so that raw session identifiers are not shared.
As a Host developer, I want unsupported cache lifetimes described explicitly, so that a routing hint does not imply a retention guarantee.
As a Host operator, I want versioned RMB-to-USD prices, so that Chinese prices cannot be interpreted as dollar rates.
As a Host operator, I want long-context price tiers tested, so that estimates remain correct at threshold boundaries.
As a Host operator, I want unsupported priority requests rejected, so that an unpriced service tier cannot create misleading estimates.
As a Host operator, I want subscription usage distinguished from estimated standard API cost, so that estimates are not presented as M Plan deductions.
As a Host developer, I want sampling and callbacks applied in the existing order, so that request customization remains predictable.
As a tenant administrator, I want final requests revalidated after hooks, so that native payloads cannot bypass model or authorization constraints.
As a Host developer, I want immutable request snapshots, so that later map mutations cannot change an active call.
As a Host developer, I want unsupported stop and format controls rejected, so that ignored fields cannot imply enforced behavior.
As a Host operator, I want default zero retries and explicit bounded initial retries, so that duplicate generation is controlled.
As a Host operator, I want permanent quota failures distinguished from transient throttling, so that exhausted plans are not retried indefinitely.
As a Host operator, I want no replay once streaming starts, so that partial responses are not silently generated again.
As a Host developer, I want cancellation and deadlines to settle one Result, so that my application can release work reliably.
As a Host operator, I want existing byte, queue and concurrency limits enforced, so that MiniMax cannot bypass resource policy.
As a Host developer, I want malformed streams and premature EOF reported as failures, so that partial output cannot appear complete.
As a Host developer, I want provider stop reasons and available trace IDs retained, so that failures remain diagnosable.
As a tenant administrator, I want metadata-only observation and redacted artifacts, so that keys and conversation content remain private.
As a maintainer, I want one public Client E2E seam, so that acceptance exercises the complete caller-visible behavior.
As a maintainer, I want failure scenarios recorded before implementation, so that tests drive the supported behavior.
As a maintainer, I want replayable request, stream and result artifacts, so that acceptance can be checked without new paid calls.
As a maintainer, I want each model and protocol to produce its own live evidence, so that shared adapters cannot substitute for independent proof.
As a maintainer, I want bounded experiments for documentation conflicts, so that unknown behavior is resolved with attributable evidence.
As a maintainer, I want fixed pi differential or extension records, so that compatibility claims reflect the actual frozen route.
As a maintainer, I want M3.1 marked as outside the frozen model catalog, so that new behavior cannot be certified by a fabricated baseline.
As a maintainer, I want DeepSeek and GLM regressions covered, so that capability refactoring preserves their established contracts.
As a maintainer, I want controlled captures distinguished from live execution, so that replay cannot be reported as fresh support.
As a maintainer, I want source and catalog applicability checked, so that stale captures cannot certify changed execution code.
As a maintainer, I want additive release requirements, so that MiniMax cannot weaken existing providers' release gates.
As a Host developer, I want complete local and cloud configuration examples, so that both deployments use the same authorization contract.
As a Host operator, I want reversible configuration and software releases, so that MiniMax can be disabled without silent rerouting.
As a maintainer, I want architecture decisions and evidence limits recorded, so that future changes preserve their context.
As a maintainer, I want all six formal or candidate identities accounted for at delivery, so that missing access cannot be hidden by narrowing the report.
